ImageDescription.value: This photo goes back a few years...actually, I just emptied my old photosig account, and thought I should feature this photo here instead. It was taken on a Sinar 4x5. 'It doesn't look like a 4x5 inches' you say, and of course, you're right; you're looking at 3 4x5 frames merged into one image. I shot a 360 panorama, and then stitched all 12 images together, but I prefer focusing on these three frames. It was taken as a challenge to find an "uncharacteristic perspective" for a postcard of the city of Toronto. The Royal York Hotel and Union Station are two of the most majestic buildings in the city, and while this photo doesn't glamorize Union Station much, I do like it as a rooftop shot. I also really like the building far off in the distance, which looks rather like a ship to me. The shot really deserves to be taken with the Xpan, and NOT 4x5 stitched images! None the less, hope you enjoy!

Artist.value: Jason V from Vancouver, Canada

ImageDescription.value: Signage in the Toronto Railway Museum about the former glory of Toronto Union Station. Though the station still stands, it is all but a mere shadow of it's former glory. This sign is self explanatory if viewed in full screen mode. Briefly however, built between 1915 and 1930, but opened officially in 1927, the beaux-arts Toronto Union station with it's spectacular Great Hall is one of the most cherished landmarks in Canada. Pictures of the actual station building itself and more notes appeared earlier on in this album. (Toronto, Canada, Nov.2015)

ImageDescription.value: This picture of a section of the sign you saw in the previous picture shows four immaculately turned out locomotives in the steam loco shed just outside Toronto Union station with the Royal York Hotel in the background. Notes about the Toronto Union station as well as the Royal York Hotel appeared earlier in his album. Although still a grand edifice, passenger services have declined a great deal and Union is now essentially mostly a commuter train terminus. The few long distance trains that do leave here are a mere 3 - 5 cars long. Sad. (Toronto, Canada, Nov.2015)

ImageDescription.value:
"10 Scents"

Union Station, Exterior, Lower Level; Artist: Chih-Chien Wang,

Before entering a portable toilet, people tend to brace themselves for what they are about to inhale. The 10 fixtures of this piece, however, are designed for more poetic than practical purposes. Filled with unlikely materials and scents, their aromas conjure up landscapes, characters and events from Lewis Carroll's classic fantasy and logic-twister "Alices's Adventures in Wonderland."

Artist.value: Randolph Croft

Categories.value: Union Station (Toronto)|Flickr images reviewed by FlickreviewR 2|Files from Randolph Croft Flickr stream

ImageDescription.value: The Great Hall, Union Station, Heather Nicol. Dislocated from her home in NY after the events of September 11, Nicol's work reflects on the vicissitudes of memory, loss and desire. The historic Union Station is the arena for countless stories of last-minute escapes, missed connections, lovers' reunions, hitting the road and being run out of town.

Artist.value: Randolph Croft
